name: Theft of service (service obtained by deception, threat or false token; less than $100)
conduct: Intentionally or knowingly securing performance of the service by deception, threat or false token. A broken promise alone, without other evidence of intent or knowledge, is insufficient to establish the deception defined in §31.01(1)(E). The actor must intend to avoid payment AND know the service is provided only for compensation. Service includes labor/professional, telecommunications/utilities/transportation, lodging/restaurant/entertainment, and supplied property for use. Value follows §31.08; consideration or a legal interest proved by a preponderance is deducted. Unascertainable value is deemed $750 to less than $2,500. Amounts from one scheme or continuing course may be aggregated under §31.09. The postdated-check defense in (g) requires that the service was secured with that check and the provider or another person presented it before its date. Presumptions do not automatically prove intent: §2.05(a) requires the underlying facts beyond a reasonable doubt, permits the jury to decline the inference, and preserves proof of other elements. Nonpayment presumptions generally use ten days after a qualifying demand; (b)(4) return periods are five/three/two days for property worth under $2,500 / $2,500 to under $10,000 / at least $10,000. The (b)(5) rent-to-own presumption requires fewer than three complete payments and nonreturn within five business days, excluding Sundays and state/federal holidays; (d-4) permits rebuttal by intent to return and inability to return. Under (d), receipt is presumed within two days, except five days for (b)(4)(A)-(B) and (b)(5).
penalty: Class C misdemeanor: ordinarily a fine up to $500; no confinement as the ordinary punishment. This choice requires stolen-service value of less than $100. H.B. 3463 changed notice rules effective September 1, 2025; if any offense element predates that date, earlier law governs. The value grades were not first created by that notice amendment. Qualifying repeat-offender and other sentencing findings require separate analysis; none is presumed.

Under (d-2), a personal/family/household-use agreement automatically renewable with each payment after its initial period and permitting ownership is excluded from this branch. The value tier concerns the service stolen, not automatically the property’s replacement value. The actor must intend to avoid payment AND know the service is provided only for compensation. Service includes labor/professional, telecommunications/utilities/transportation, lodging/restaurant/entertainment, and supplied property for use. Value follows §31.08; consideration or a legal interest proved by a preponderance is deducted. Unascertainable value is deemed $750 to less than $2,500. Amounts from one scheme or continuing course may be aggregated under §31.09. The postdated-check defense in (g) requires that the service was secured with that check and the provider or another person presented it before its date. Presumptions do not automatically prove intent: §2.05(a) requires the underlying facts beyond a reasonable doubt, permits the jury to decline the inference, and preserves proof of other elements. Nonpayment presumptions generally use ten days after a qualifying demand; (b)(4) return periods are five/three/two days for property worth under $2,500 / $2,500 to under $10,000 / at least $10,000. The (b)(5) rent-to-own presumption requires fewer than three complete payments and nonreturn within five business days, excluding Sundays and state/federal holidays; (d-4) permits rebuttal by intent to return and inability to return. Under (d), receipt is presumed within two days, except five days for (b)(4)(A)-(B) and (b)(5).
penalty: Class B misdemeanor: ordinarily up to 180 days in jail, a fine up to $2,000, or both. This choice requires stolen-service value of $100 or more but less than $750. H.B. 3463 changed notice rules effective September 1, 2025; if any offense element predates that date, earlier law governs. The value grades were not first created by that notice amendment. Qualifying repeat-offender and other sentencing findings require separate analysis; none is presumed.

name: Forgery (other writing; ordinary grade)
conduct: Forging a writing with intent to defraud or harm another. Under (a)(1), this means making/altering/authenticating a writing purporting to be another’s unauthorized act, an incorrect time/place/sequence, or a copy with no original; issuing/passing/otherwise uttering such a forged writing; or possessing it with intent to utter it. Mere possession without that intent is not the possession branch. Writing includes recorded information, money, listed symbols and instruments. A writing outside the special types in (d)/(e), with the (e-1) property/service-purpose value ladder not applicable. This choice uses the grade without the elderly-victim increase. If the offense is shown committed against an individual age 65 or older, (e-2) raises it one category, except (e-1)(6) remains first degree.
